Unpack the definition and record what the data are. items.title: Induction and restriction bimodules for KLR algebras
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $ eta,\gamma\in Q_+$ put $e( eta,\gamma):=\sum_{
u\in I^{ eta},
u'\in I^{\gamma}}e(
u\ast
u')\in R( eta+\gamma)$, where $
u\ast
u'$ is concatenation; this is an idempotent. The block inclusions $R( eta)\hookrightarrow R( eta+\gamma)$, $r\mapsto r\otimes1$ and $R(\gamma)\hookrightarrow R( eta+\gamma)$, $s\mapsto1\otimes s$ combine into an injective $k$-algebra map $R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)	o R( eta+\gamma)$ whose image is $e( eta,\gamma)R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)$; in the diagram calculus it is horizontal concatenation of diagrams. **Induction** and **restriction** are the functors on graded left modules
$$\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M oxtimes N):=R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)\otimes_{R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)}(M\otimes_kN),\qquad \mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}L:=e( eta,\gamma)L,$$
where $\otimes_{R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)}$ is the graded balanced tensor product of [[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] (total-degree grading) and $M\otimes_kN$ carries the graded tensor product structure. Both functors are additive and degree-zero on degree-zero maps and extend to the direct sums over weights; the $R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)$-side is a graded $(R( eta+\gamma),R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma))$-bimodule and $e( eta,\gamma)R( eta+\gamma)$ is its right-module counterpart, so the two tensor functors are of the two HA-18 sidedness types. Shifts satisfy $\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M\{r\} oxtimes N\{s\})\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M oxtimes N)\{r+s\}$ and $\mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}(L\{r\})\cong(\mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}L)\{r\}$ ([[lem-graded-balanced-tensor-and-shift-isomorphisms]]). For a partial flag $ eta= eta_1+\cdots+ eta_r$ the iterated functors are defined by iteration, and the parenthesization-independent identification is the one consumed below.
items.strategy:
Only the well-definedness and convention checks are owed. The map $R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)	o R( eta+\gamma)$ is defined on the free product of the two block subalgebras; the idempotent relation (1) of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] gives $e( eta,\gamma)^2=e( eta,\gamma)$ and $e(
u\ast
u')(R( eta)\otimes R(\gamma))e(\eta\ast\eta')
e0$ only for $
u=\eta,
u'=\eta'$, so the image lies in the corner and the map is injective by the PBW basis of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] restricted to separated diagrams. The balanced tensor products exist by HA-18 (the balance relations are homogeneous), and the shift identities are the shift lemmas of HA-18 applied to the two tensor factors. The sidedness dictionary: $R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)$ is a graded $(R( eta+\gamma),R( eta)\otimes R(\gamma))$-bimodule and is used as the kernel of a functor from left $R( eta)\otimes R(\gamma)$-modules to left $R( eta+\gamma)$-modules; $e( eta,\gamma)R( eta+\gamma)$ is the mirror kernel used for restriction. This is KL I §2.6 read with HA-18's graded balanced tensors; no choice principle is used.

items.title: The PBW (monomial) basis theorem for KLR algebras
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix a reduced-expression system: for each $w\in S_n$ one reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$, and for $
u\in I^n$ put $	au_w:=	au_{i_1}\cdots	au_{i_r}\in R_n(Q)$. Then the monomials $	au_wx_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}e(
u)$, over all $w\in S_n$, $a_1,\dots,a_n\ge0$ and $
u\in I^n$, form a $k$-basis of $R_n(Q)$; equivalently $R_n(Q)$ is a free $k$-module on these monomials, and $R( eta)$ has the corresponding basis. Moreover each $R( eta)$ has finite-dimensional homogeneous components, and the graded dimension of the summand $e(
u)R_n(Q)e(
u')$ is the polynomial counting the monomials, so the graded ranks are independent of the parameters $Q$: $\dim_kR_n(Q)_m<\infty$ for all $m$ and $R_n(Q)_m=0$ for $m\ll0$. In particular $R( eta)$ is a locally finite graded algebra and $R( eta)_0=k\,e( eta)$.
items.strategy:
Two routes are available and both are complete; the author uses the second for the general datum and may check the first. **(a) Simply-laced (KL I).** Theorem 2.5 produces the basis of $_jR(
u)_i$ directly from the faithful polynomial representation and the straightening of diagrams; Corollary 2.6 gives faithfulness. **(b) General datum (Rouquier).** The generating set $S=\{	au_{i_1,s_{i_2}\cdots s_{i_r}(
u)}\cdots	au_{i_r,
u}x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}e(
u)\}$ introduced in §3.2.1 spans by an induction on the defining relations; the faithful representation of [[thm-polynomial-representation-of-a-klr-algebra]] supplies a $k$-linear map that separates $S$, so $S$ is independent; hence it is a basis. Independence of parameters follows because $S$ is defined by reduced words and dots only, and the relations used in the spanning argument are homogeneous of the fixed degrees ([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]), so the graded components are the spans of the monomials of the corresponding degrees. The finiteness of each graded component is immediate from the fixed number of words of each degree, and vanishing for $m\ll0$ from the finiteness of $S_n$ and the lower bound $\deg	au\ge-\max_{i
e j}b_{ij}$ on each crossing. In characteristic-arbitrary $k$ the argument is unchanged; no AC is used.

items.title: Induction and restriction are exact, biadjoint and preserve finite graded projectives
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta,\gamma\in Q_+$.
(i) **Freeness.** $1_{\beta,\gamma}R(\beta+\gamma):=e(\beta,\gamma)R(\beta+\gamma)$ is a free graded left $R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)$-module with basis $\{\widetilde w\}$ indexed by the minimal length representatives $w$ of the left cosets of $S_{|\beta|}\times S_{|\gamma|}$ in $S_{|\beta|+|\gamma|}$, each $\widetilde w$ a sum of staircase diagrams over the words of $\beta,\gamma$; its rank is $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$.
(ii) **Exactness.** $\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}$ and $\mathrm{Res}_{\beta,\gamma}$ are exact functors between the graded module categories.
(iii) **Frobenius reciprocity.** $\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{Res}_{\beta,\gamma}$: there is a natural degree-zero bijection $\mathrm{Hom}_{R(\beta+\gamma)}(\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N),L)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{R(\beta)\otimes R(\gamma)}(M\boxtimes N,\mathrm{Res}_{\beta,\gamma}L)$.
(iv) **Biadjunction.** $\mathrm{Res}_{\beta,\gamma}$ is also left adjoint to $\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}$; the unit and counit are the cup and cap diagrams built from the closing-diagram trace $t$ on $R(\beta+\gamma)$ of the Frobenius form over the center, and are compatible with the grading up to the shifts recorded in $t$. Here $t$ is the degree-normalized linear form on $R(\beta+\gamma)$ given on the PBW basis by the coefficient of the longest word $w_0$ (the closing-diagram functional), with the scalar normalization adjusted on the two-colour crossings so that it is symmetrizing; the exact normalization is pinned at authoring against KL §2.2 and Webster §1.3.
(v) **Projectives.** $\mathrm{Res}_{\beta,\gamma}$ and $\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}$ carry finite graded projective modules to finite graded projective modules.
All assertions are functorial in $M,N,L$ and compatible with the grading shifts of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]].
items.strategy: Follow the sources in order. (i) is KL I Proposition 2.16 with its explicit basis of staircases and the coset count; the same basis is displayed in KK Corollary 3.4's decomposition. (ii) $\mathrm{Res}$ is exact because idempotent multiplication is exact; $\mathrm{Ind}$ is exact by the HA-18 tensor exactness theorem applied to the kernel $R(\beta+\gamma)e(\beta,\gamma)$, which is flat as a right $R(\beta)\otimes R(\gamma)$-module because it is free by (i). (iii) is the standard adjunction of $M\mapsto Ae\otimes_BM$ and $N\mapsto eN$ for a ring inclusion $B\hookrightarrow A$ with $e$ idempotent (KL I §2.6, opening paragraph; KK (3.12)) reformulated in the graded setting via the HA-18 tensor-Hom adjunction. (iv) The closing-diagram functional is well defined and homogeneous on the PBW basis of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]; cyclicity $t(ab)=t(ba)$ is checked on the two-colour crossings with the adjusted scalar so that the result is symmetric (Webster §1.3, Theorem 1.8 and Remark 1.9, in the generic/idempotent-corner form), and Rouquier §2.3.2 supplies the equivalence between a Frobenius form and an adjunction of the extension/restriction pair; this produces the natural bijections $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathrm{Res}L,M)\cong\mathrm{Hom}(L,\mathrm{Ind}M)$ and the compatible cup/cap morphisms. (v) For $\mathrm{Res}$: if $P$ is a degree-zero summand of a finite sum of shifts of $R(\beta+\gamma)$, then $\mathrm{Res}P$ is a degree-zero summand of a finite sum of shifts of $1_{\beta,\gamma}R(\beta+\gamma)$, which is free, hence projective, by (i) and HA-18's projective-preservation theorem (KL I Corollary 2.17). For $\mathrm{Ind}$: it is a left adjoint of the exact $\mathrm{Res}$ by (iii), and a left adjoint of an exact functor carries projectives to projectives; or, directly, HA-18's tensor theorem applies since $R(\beta+\gamma)e(\beta,\gamma)$ is finite graded projective as a left $R(\beta+\gamma)$-module. items.title: Nil-Hecke idempotents and divided-power KLR projectives
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$. Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift one has $R(n\alpha_i)\cong P_{i,n}^{\oplus[n]_{q_i}!}$ with $[n]_{q_i}!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^a-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$, so $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks; then $[P_\theta]$ depends only on the multiset of divided powers (not on the chosen sequence of colors) exactly as the source relations for the half dictate, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.
items.strategy: Well-definedness. (i) $R(n\alpha_i)$ is the nil-Hecke algebra by the relations of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] specialized to $Q_{ii}=0$; the PBW basis of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] is $\{x^a\tau_w\}$, so the span of $\{x^a\tau_w\}$ is everything. (ii) $\partial_{w_0}$ is independent of the reduced expression by the braid relations, and $e_{i,n}^2=e_{i,n}$ is the standard nil-Hecke idempotent computation: $\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$ is the image of the symmetrizing operator, and the divided-difference identities move the $x$'s through the crossings; the same computation gives $\psi(e_{i,n})^2=\psi(e_{i,n})$. (iii) Nonvanishing: in the PBW basis the monomial $x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}\tau_{w_0}$ has leading coefficient $1$ and cannot cancel. (iv) The module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation of the nil-Hecke algebra (KL I §2.2), hence projective and indecomposable; the displayed decomposition into $[n]_{q_i}!$ copies after the shift is KL's example computation, and $\mathrm{End}_0=k$ is the degree-0 part of that computation (a degree-zero endomorphism of a projective with one-dimensional top is scalar). (v) For several colours, $P_\theta$ is defined by induction along the block embedding of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; the order-independence claimed for the class (not for the module) is the categorical content of the commutativity of the divided powers of distinct colours, proved with [[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]] and the standard tensor decomposition. The construction is choice-free; no AC is used.

items.title: Graded Krull-Schmidt and shift-orbit bases for finitely generated KLR modules
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique up to isomorphism and grading shifts; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the polynomial subalgebra, and remains simple after forgetting the grading; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the classes of simples and their projective covers are dual bases under the Hom pairing of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].
items.strategy: Regard $R(\beta)$ as a finite module over the polynomial subalgebra $\mathrm{Pol}(\beta)=\bigoplus_{\nu}k[x_1,\dots,x_n]e(\nu)$, which is free of rank $|\beta|!$ by the basis [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] and is a polynomial ring; note $\mathrm{Pol}(\beta)$ is a noetherian graded commutative ring. Then $R(\beta)$ is a noetherian graded ring and finitely generated graded modules have the graded Fitting decomposition: the endomorphism ring of an indecomposable finitely generated graded module is local after factoring out the grading, and the standard graded Krull-Schmidt argument (Fitting's lemma run on homogeneous idempotents) gives (i). For (ii): a simple graded module $S$ is annihilated by $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ because the center acts by a graded field and a nonzero central action would admit a proper cyclic submodule; since $R(\beta)/\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)R(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional (of graded dimension $(|\beta|!)^2$ in the notation of the sources), $S$ is finite-dimensional and there are finitely many simples; projective covers exist because finite-dimensional graded algebras have graded projective covers (HA-19). For (iii): the Krull-Schmidt decomposition makes $K_0$ and $G_0$ free on shift orbits, exactly as in the finite-dimensional case handled by [[thm-graded-projective-and-simple-classes-have-shift-orbit-bases]]; the duality of the two bases is the Hom pairing [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]. The source KL I §2.5 states the Krull-Schmidt property and the freeness of $G_0$ directly; this item supplies the local proof and the matching K_0 statement. No AC is used.

items.title: The KLR Grothendieck ring satisfies the divided-power quantum Serre relations
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $K_0(R):=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}K_0(R(\beta))$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective modules with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]).
(i) The induction product $[P][P']:=[\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(P\boxtimes P')]$ for $P\in K_0(R(\beta)),P'\in K_0(R(\gamma))$ makes $K_0(R)$ a unital associative $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra, and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ makes it a coassociative counital $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-coalgebra; with the twisted multiplication on $K_0(R)\otimes K_0(R)$ defined by $(x_1\otimes x_2)(x_1'\otimes x_2')=q^{-|x_2||x_1'|}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ on homogeneous elements, $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism ([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]], KL I Propositions 3.1-3.2).
(ii) With the divided-power projectives $P_{i,n}$ of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], the classes $[P_{i,n}]$ satisfy, for all $i\ne j$, the divided-power quantum Serre relation
$$\sum_{a+b=-a_{ij}+1}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}]\,[P_{j,1}]\,[P_{i,b}]=0\qquad\text{in }K_0(R),$$
with the convention $[P_{i,0}]=1=[P_{j,0}]$, and satisfy $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$ when $a_{ij}=0$; these are the defining relations of the negative half.
(iii) Consequently the assignment $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ of the divided-power form of the negative half, with $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ and $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$; $\gamma$ is compatible with the coproducts ($r$ on $A f$ and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ on $K_0(R)$) and with the bar involutions, and it is $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear.
items.strategy: (i) Associativity is the parenthesization independence of iterated induction (HA-18 shift/associativity lemmas plus [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]); unitality uses $R(0)=k$ and $\mathrm{Ind}_{0,\beta}=1$; coassociativity is Mackey's formula (KL I Proposition 2.18). The twisted multiplication is fixed by $|x|\in Q$ and the standard sign-free twist of KL I (3.1). (ii) The categorical content is that the divided-power projectives decompose according to the quantum Serre relations: for $i\ne j$ and $d=-a_{ij}$, KL II Proposition 6 exhibits isomorphisms of graded projective modules $\bigoplus_{a\ \mathrm{even}}P_{i(a)ji(d-a)}\cong\bigoplus_{a\ \mathrm{odd}}P_{i(a)ji(d-a)}$ (with the multi-dot convention for multiple edges), and KL I Proposition 2.13 is the simply-laced case; taking classes and using the identification $[P_{i(a)ji(d-a)}]=[P_{i,a}][P_{j,1}][P_{i,d-a}]$ from [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] gives the relation. The commutation for $a_{ij}=0$ is the intersection isomorphism for two non-adjacent colours. (iii) By (ii) the kernel of the free-algebra surjection $T(\theta_i)\to K_0(R)$ contains the Serre ideal; the negative half $A f$ is the quotient of the free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra by the divided-power Serre ideal ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[thm-the-formal-quantum-serre-half-embeds-in-the-quantum-shuffle-algebra-and-is-degreewise-free]] together with the RL-12 Serre presentation), so the surjection descends; barredness and coproduct compatibility are checked on generators as in KL I Proposition 3.4. No AC is used.

items.title: The KLR Cartan (graded Hom) pairing on the projective Grothendieck group
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finite graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$(\ [P],[Q]\ )_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finite graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=\overline{([P],[Q])_\beta}$ under the bar involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, so the first pairing is symmetric and the second is the bar-conjugate sesquilinear version. Both pairings are additive in each variable, compatible with shifts $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$ as a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-bilinear pairing $(\ ,\ ):K_0(R)\times K_0(R)\to\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1},(\beta)_q^{-1}]$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the center. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$.
items.strategy: Well-definedness: $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a graded vector space of finite dimension in each degree and bounded below, so $\mathrm{gdim}$ is a well-defined element of $\mathbb Z((q))$; freeness over the polynomial/center subalgebra (KL I §2.5, using the basis [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]) upgrades it to $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$. Symmetry of the first pairing is the commutativity $P^\psi\otimes_{R}Q\cong Q^\psi\otimes_RP$ of the balanced tensor, and the identity $([P],[Q])'=\overline{([P],[Q])}$ is the standard hom-tensor comparison $\operatorname{HOM}(P,Q)\cong$ the tensor form conjugated by the grading reversal, as in KL I (2.41)-(2.47) and §3.4; the additive and sesquilinear properties are HA-19's pairing theorems transported along the identifications of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. The generator values follow from $P_i=R(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]$, $P_i^\psi\otimes_{R(\alpha_i)}P_i\cong k[x_1]$ as a graded vector space with $\deg x_1=2d_i$ (KL I Proposition 3.3 and the computation $([P_i],[P_i])=\mathrm{gdim}(k[x])=(1-q^2)^{-1}$ in the simply-laced normalization). The convention for $\psi$ is recorded explicitly because it fixes the sign of the shift of the hom form; no AC is used.

items.title: The KLR category categorifies the negative quantum half
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] over any field $k$. Then the homomorphism $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]] is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebras and of $\mathbb N[I]$-graded twisted bialgebras:
(i) **Surjectivity.** Every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear combination of classes of divided-power projectives $[P_\theta]$, $\theta$ a sequence of divided powers of weight $\beta$; hence $\gamma$ is onto.
(ii) **Injectivity.** $\gamma$ is injective, because it preserves the forms by [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]] and the source form $B_L$ (equivalently $B_K$) is nondegenerate on each finite weight component.
(iii) **Compatibility.** $\gamma$ intertwines the multiplications ($[\mathrm{Ind}]$ against the product in $A f$), the comultiplications ($[\mathrm{Res}]$ against $r$), the bar involutions and the forms; the graded ranks of $R(\beta)$ match the ranks of $A f_\beta$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]), so the weightwise isomorphism is also a graded-dimension isomorphism.
Equivalently, $K_0(R)$ is a free $A$-module with the classes of the indecomposable graded projective $R$-modules as a shift-orbit basis ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]), and the divided-power classes that appear in the surjectivity clause form an $A$-basis.

items.statement: Assume the Cartan datum of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] is symmetric (so all $d_i=1$ and $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$), the field $k$ has characteristic $0$, and the KLR parameters are the quiver-geometric ones (the specialization $H_n(\Gamma)$ attached to a quiver without loops or multiple edges, with the standard choice $Q_{ij}(u,v)=u+v$ on the edges; equivalently the geometric parameters of the quiver-variety construction). Then, normalizing each indecomposable finitely generated graded projective $R(\beta)$-module to be self-dual for the duality $\psi$ ($P\cong P^\psi$ up to the fixed shift), the map $b\mapsto[P_b]$ is a bijection between the lower global basis $B(\infty)$ of the negative half ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]) and the shift-orbit basis of $K_0(R)$ by self-dual indecomposable projectives; under the isomorphism $\gamma$ of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] one has $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for the lower global lift $G(b)$, and the identification is compatible with the based quotient of [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]]. items.title: Degenerate parameters Q_ij destroy the faithful polynomial-representation route
items.statement:
**Statement refuted:** the faithful polynomial-representation route to the PBW basis and the Grothendieck-ring comparison of [[thm-polynomial-representation-of-a-klr-algebra]] needs only the hermitian symmetry (Q2) and the degree condition (Q3); the nonvanishing conditions (Q1) and (Q4) can be dropped.
**Counterexample (two vertices).** Let $I=\{i,j\}$, $a_{ij}=-1$, and take the degenerate parameters $Q_{ij}=Q_{ji}=0$, which satisfy (Q2) and (Q3) but not (Q1). Then:
(a) $R(\alpha_i+\alpha_j)$ is still a free $k$-module with spanning set $\{x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1^\varepsilon e(\nu)\}$, but no factorization $Q_{ij}(u,v)=P_{ij}(u,v)P_{ji}(v,u)$ with nonzero factors exists, so every algebra map from $R(\alpha_i+\alpha_j)$ into $\mathrm{End}(k[x_1,x_2]e(ij)\oplus k[x_1,x_2]e(ji))$ which sends $x_a$ to multiplication and $\tau_1$ to $P_{ij}(x_2,x_1)s_1$ on the $ij$-component must send $\tau_1$ to $0$, because $\tau_1^2$ would have to be both $0=Q_{ij}$ and $P_{ij}(x_1,x_2)P_{ji}(x_2,x_1)$.
(b) Consequently the constructed polynomial action is not faithful: the image of the degree-$1$ component $k\tau_1e(ij)\oplus k\tau_1e(ji)$ is zero, while $\tau_1\ne0$ in the algebra.
(c) Dropping the hermitian symmetry (Q2) while keeping (Q1), (Q3) and (Q4) also destroys the basis route: for $a_{ij}=-1$ and the non-hermitian pair $Q_{ij}(u,v)=u+2v$, $Q_{ji}(u,v)=u+v$ (both homogeneous of degree $2$ with nonzero extremal coefficients, but $Q_{ji}(v,u)=v+u\ne u+2v$), associativity together with relation (4) on the two corners $(i,j)$ and $(j,i)$ and the dot slides of (6) for the pair of distinct residues gives the identity $\bigl(Q_{ji}(x_1,x_2)-Q_{ij}(x_2,x_1)\bigr)\tau_1e(ij)=-x_1\tau_1e(ij)=0$, hence $\tau_1x_2e(ij)=0$; the spanning monomial $\tau_1x_2e(ij)$ of Rouquier's family $\{x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1^\varepsilon e(\nu)\}$ therefore vanishes, so that family is not linearly independent and the graded PBW statement fails. Equivalently, Rouquier's Theorem 3.7 shows that PBW is equivalent to $Q_{ij}(u,v)=Q_{ji}(v,u)$, the identity violated here. (On $(i,j,i)$ the braid relation reads $\bigl(\tau_2\tau_1\tau_2-\tau_1\tau_2\tau_1\bigr)e(i,j,i)=-e(i,j,i)$: both sides have degree $0$, so the failure is a linear dependence, not a degree mismatch.)
Thus both the nonvanishing hypotheses and the hermitian symmetry are load-bearing for the basis and rank arguments; the example does not claim that the KLR algebra with $Q_{ij}=0$ fails to be free (PBW independence has its own source proof), only that the faithful polynomial-representation route used in this library collapses.

items.title: The KLR algebras in root degrees alpha_i and two alpha_i
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix $i\in I$.
(a) In weight $\alpha_i$ there is one sequence, and $R(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]e(i)$: the only relations are that $x_1$ is central, so $\{x_1^a\}_{a\ge0}$ is a $k$-basis, $\deg x_1=2d_i$, and $\mathrm{gdim}\,R(\alpha_i)=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}$. The algebra is commutative; up to shift its unique simple module is $k$ with $x_1$ acting by $0$, $R(\alpha_i)$ is the projective cover of that simple, and $[R(\alpha_i)]=[P_{i,1}]$ with $([P_{i,1}],[P_{i,1}])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}$.
(b) In weight $2\alpha_i$ one has $R(2\alpha_i)\cong NH_2$, the nil Hecke algebra of rank $2$, with $k$-basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,\ x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1\}_{a,b\ge0}$, free of rank $2$ over $k[x_1,x_2]$, and relations (in the normalization of relation (6) of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]])
$$\tau_1^2=0,\qquad \tau_1x_1=x_2\tau_1+e(ii),\qquad \tau_1x_2=x_1\tau_1-e(ii).$$
Its graded dimension is $\dfrac{1+q^{-2d_i}}{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}$, and the element $e_{i,2}=x_1\tau_1$ is a nonzero idempotent of degree $0$ with $P_{i,2}=R(2\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,2})\{-d_i\}$ an indecomposable projective of class $[P_{i,2}]=\gamma(\theta_i^{(2)})$ in $K_0(R)$.
items.strategy: (a) The PBW basis of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] for the single sequence $(i)$ is $\{x_1^a\}$; centrality is relation (2) and there is no crossing for $n=1$. The simple module and cover statements are the standard theory of $k[x_1]$ together with [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]; the pairing value is the normalization of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]]. (b) For two strands of one colour the PBW basis is $\{x_1^ax_2^b,x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1\}$ and the relations are relations (4) and (6) specialized to $Q_{ii}=0$ and $\nu_1=\nu_2$; the grading gives the two geometric series $\frac1{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}+\frac{q^{-2d_i}}{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}$. For the idempotent: $\tau_1x_1=x_2\tau_1+e(ii)$ gives $e_{i,2}^2=x_1\tau_1x_1\tau_1=x_1(x_2\tau_1+e(ii))\tau_1=x_1x_2\tau_1^2+x_1\tau_1=x_1\tau_1$ using $\tau_1^2=0$, so $e_{i,2}^2=e_{i,2}$; nonvanishing is read off the PBW basis. Indecomposability and the class identification are the $n=2$ cases of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. No AC is used.

items.title: The nil-Hecke divided-power projective in rank two
items.statement:
Work in $R(2\alpha_i)\cong NH_2$ of [[ex-klr-algebras-in-root-degrees-alpha-i-and-two-alpha-i]]: generators $x_1,x_2$ of degree $2d_i$ and $\tau=\tau_1$ of degree $-2d_i$, the basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,x_1^ax_2^b\tau\}$, the relations $\tau^2=0$, $\tau x_1=x_2\tau+e$, $\tau x_2=x_1\tau-e$, and center $k[x_1,x_2]^{S_2}$. Then:
(a) $e_{i,2}:=x_1\tau$ is a nonzero idempotent of degree $0$ and $\psi(e_{i,2})=\tau x_1$ is the reflected idempotent; the module $P_{i,2}:=R(2\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,2})\{-d_i\}$ is the polynomial representation of $NH_2$, an indecomposable graded projective with one-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism ring, and it is the projective cover of the unique simple $R(2\alpha_i)$-module up to shift.
(b) $R(2\alpha_i)\cong P_{i,2}^{\oplus[2]_{q_i}!}$ with $[2]_{q_i}!=(q_i+q_i^{-1})$, so $P_{i,2}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift.
(c) In $K_0(R)$, $[P_{i,2}]=\gamma(\theta_i^{(2)})$ for the divided power $\theta_i^{(2)}=F_i^2/[2]_{q_i}$, and its self-pairing is $([P_{i,2}],[P_{i,2}])=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}(1-q_i^4)^{-1}$, the value of the Lusztig-normalized form at $\theta_i^{(2)}$.
items.strategy: (a) Compute $e_{i,2}^2=x_1\tau x_1\tau=x_1(x_2\tau+e)\tau=x_1x_2\tau^2+x_1\tau=x_1\tau$ using $\tau^2=0$; nonvanishing is read off the PBW basis. The reflected element satisfies $\psi(e_{i,2})^2=(\tau x_1)(\tau x_1)=(x_2\tau+e)\tau x_1=x_2\tau^2x_1+\tau x_1=\tau x_1=\psi(e_{i,2})$ using $\tau^2=0$, so both are idempotents of degree $0$ (the $x$-monomial has degree $2d_i$ and $\tau$ has degree $-2d_i$). The left ideal $R(2\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,2})$ is the polynomial representation by the rank-one case of [[thm-polynomial-representation-of-a-klr-algebra]]; it is indecomposable projective, hence the projective cover of its (unique) simple head, and its degree-zero endomorphism ring is $k$ because the degree-zero part of the polynomial representation is one-dimensional. (b) The decomposition into $[2]_{q_i}!$ copies is the rank-two case of the source computation $NH_m\cong P_m^{\oplus[m]_{q_i}!}$; uniqueness of the indecomposable summand up to shift follows from the Krull-Schmidt property [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]] together with the single indecomposable class. (c) The class identification is the $n=2$ case of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] (see also [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]), and the self-pairing is the rank-one value $\prod_{a=1}^{2}(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$ of [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]]. No AC is used.
